Hi! Ever wanted to play DDR at home? You may have tried one of the many home console (CS) versions and been underwhelmed by the choice of songs. How you would like to have hundreds of songs? Or thousands?? What you need is Stepmania.

This is a short guide to getting started with Stepmania. Feel free to chime in with anything you feel I may have missed, or to ask anything if you are not sure.

Things you need: A PC.

Yep, that's it. Stepmania can be played simply with the arrow keys on your keyboard. Now this in itself is not the best way to emulate the arcade experience; but it is a great way to practice playing the game. Timing and reading comprehension can be greatly enhanced by playing this way.

Now obviously, you are going to need a dance mat to bring this to the next level. What you buy is sadly more to do with what you can find than anything else these days. Some people will find plastic mats are perfectly fine for their abilities and/or surroundings; whilst other folks will want to try and find metal mats to more accurately bring the arcade experience home.

If you can, always buy a mat that has USB and is advertised as being PC friendly. Whilst you can find a plethora of adaptors online for every controller ever made, you will soon discover that your biggest enemy when creating the best possible Stepmania setup is timing latency. Lag, even of hundredths of a second, can completely ruin the experience of playing.

You can download Stepmania from here .

At the time of writing this guide, Stepmania is currently at version 5.06. It's a small download, of around 50 MB. Get it installed and fire it up. The whole process should take less than 5 minutes if you have a reasonable connection to the internet.

Now that you have Stepmania, you need songs to fill it with! Whilst there are hundreds of resources for such things; for the purposes of this guide I would recommend Zenius-I-Vanisher .

Once you have downloaded some songs or packs of songs, you need to unzip them.

Inside the Stepmania folder you will find a folder called Songs. Inside of that directory you will need to create further folders. The structure works like this. SONGS - ALBUM - FILES

So for example, you might have Songs - DDR Extreme - A

Inside the folder - A - you will have the song itself (usually in mp3 format), and the stepfile itself. You may also find picture files like PNG or JPG which are for the banner of the song and the song's background image whilst you play.

Once you have this folder structure setup, you are ready to go! If you are using a keyboard to play, just load up Stepmania and have fun! If you have a mat, you will need to set it up a little first. In the options menu, you will find key configs. Enter this screen and change the configs for the UP, LEFT, RIGHT, DOWN, START, and BACK buttons to the ones on your mat. Some mats may only have four buttons. In this case just change the directions. You can continue to use the keyboard to select items and to backup from menus.

This should be enough to get you started. If you need any help, please don't hesitiate to ask. There is no such thing as a silly question. Only silly answers.
